Container.Name: Stackyard
Container.Overview: A self-hosted homelab dashboard you actually want to look at.[br][br]Most dashboards are a wall of numbers and charts. Stackyard is the opposite: a calm, launcher-style grid of app tiles, folders, and a small number of genuinely useful widgets. Built to be glanced at a hundred times a day without feeling cluttered.[br][br]Everything is set up from the browser. Add app tiles, group them into folders, arrange pages, and drop in widgets for the services you already run. Widgets cover Docker, system health, downloads, media, backups, network and more.[br][br]Runs as one container with no external database and no runtime dependencies. Configuration and uploaded icons persist in the two paths below.[br][br]Note: most homelab services live on private addresses. The Allow Private IPs setting below is on by default so links and widgets pointing at your other containers work. Turn it off to keep the SSRF guard enabled.

Container.Changes:
### 1.9.2 - 2026-09-02
### Changed
- Search on a phone now closes with a Cancel button beside the field instead of a circle at the top of the screen.
- Fetch now says that a full API URL is needed when the badge address names a host only, including when the address fails to answer.
- A badge address that redirects now says so, instead of reporting an internal error.
- Deleting an item, deleting a folder, signing out all devices and turning off password protection now ask in the app's own dialog, in the chosen language.
### Removed
- The DNS widget no longer offers a medium size. Existing medium DNS widgets become small.
### Fixed
- Settings now shows the same Unsplash wallpaper as the dashboard, instead of picking a new photo on every visit.
- The search overlay and the wallpaper source list announce their own names again, instead of names meant for other controls.
- Folder tiles and the folder overlay announce their name in the chosen language, instead of appending an English word to it.
- The analog clock's discs show the same overlap colours in every browser, instead of hiding each other and the date in Firefox.
- Settings now shows its confirmations, errors, pills, widget size names and connection-test results in the chosen language.
- Persian now uses one agreed word per concept for address, password, test and system, instead of two.
- The settings toggle, the dropdown chevron and the update dot now follow the text direction in right-to-left languages.
- Settings no longer accumulates memory as multi-select fields are redrawn.
- Folder tiles and the folder rows in Settings are real buttons, so they behave as controls for the keyboard and for screen readers.
- A screen reader can no longer read the Settings page behind an open dialog.
- A screen reader can no longer read the dashboard behind an open folder.
- A screen reader can no longer read the dashboard behind the first-run password prompt.
- A screen reader can no longer read the dashboard behind the search overlay.
- Dragging a row in Settings no longer slows down as the list grows.
- Auto-scrolling while dragging a row now moves at the same speed on every display.
- Apps in the folder picker show their icon instead of a broken image.
- Medium, large and extra-large widgets are their full width again.
- A failing badge shows why on hover or tap, instead of only in its name.
### Security
- The dashboard and settings pages no longer permit inline styles.
- A custom widget's page is sandboxed and can no longer navigate the dashboard away.
- Released images carry the operating system security patches available at build time. The step that applies them was being served from a build cache.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the dashboard is reached on.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Dashboard configuration. Keep this, or every setting is lost on update.

Config.Name: Icon Storage
Config.Description: Icons you upload for your app tiles.

Config.Name: Allow Private IPs
Config.Description: Let widgets and badges reach private addresses, which most homelab services use. Set to false to keep the SSRF guard on.

Config.Name: Docker Socket Proxy URL
Config.Description: Optional. Address of a Docker socket proxy, for the Docker widgets. Example: http://socket-proxy:2375

Config.Name: Trust Proxy
Config.Description: Optional. Set to true when running behind a reverse proxy, so client addresses are read from the forwarded headers.
